node_definition.done_when: Done when a new tests/test_a_batch_decodes_the_ledger_index_once.py builds a temporary crew home with a ledger of 200 rows and dispatches a batch of 10 entries across 3 plans. Counting wrappers on _index_payload and _last_good_index_data assert that the whole batch calls each at most once. The batch's per-entry results equal those the base revision returns for the same entries. The negative control restores a ledger load per entry, and the decode count is then at least 10. On the all_debug partition, the same 8-entry review batch shape at base and at head, against a home seeded at the live ledger-row count read at dispatch, reports the base's and the head's wall time per entry, each with its load average. The head's is lower, and the manifest states the measured ratio. The decode leaves the other profiled frames in place, so the ratio is reported, not gated. By the profile, removing seven of eight decodes cuts about 18 points of the 21% the ledger costs. Every log is under the run directory, starts with its revision and the literal command, and ends in EXIT= . The test files importing reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py add no failure against the base revision, run one arm at a time with at most -n 4 . Ruff check and ruff format --check add no findings on the staged paths. Write paths: reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py , reckon/ledger.py (which holds load , _index_payload and _last_good_index_data ), tests/test_a_batch_decodes_the_ledger_index_once.py and the node's fragment.
